# How much wallpaper do I need?

> Estimate whole wallpaper rolls from full-height drops, including trim allowance, straight or half-drop pattern repeats, and optional deductions for very wide openings.

## Calculator
- [Open the calculator](https://howmuchwallpaperdoineed.com/): US double roll: a 32 ft wall run, 8 ft ceiling, 20.5 in × 33 ft roll, 24 in straight repeat, and 4 in trim need 7 double rolls (19 drops, 10 ft cut length). Metric: a 10 m wall run, 2.4 m ceiling, 53 cm × 10.05 m rolls, 64 cm straight repeat, and 10 cm trim need 7 rolls (19 drops, 3 drops per roll).

## Guide
- [How to work out how much wallpaper you need](https://howmuchwallpaperdoineed.com/guide/): step-by-step measuring, common mistakes, and ordering checklist.

## Formula and method
Cut length = ceiling((wall height + trim) / repeat) × repeat; Drops per roll = floor(roll length / cut length) for straight match; Rolls = ceiling(ceiling((wall width − skipped openings) / roll width) / drops per roll).

Subtract only wide skipped openings from combined wall width, then divide by roll width and round up for required full-height drops. Add trimming allowance to wall height and round up to a whole pattern repeat for straight matches. For half-drop matches, each additional strip cut from the same roll adds half a pattern repeat to align adjacent panels. Divide roll length to find whole drops per roll, then round required drops divided by drops per roll up to whole rolls.

## Limits
Measure the tallest wall height. Leave skipped openings at zero for standard doors and windows because full-height strips are still needed beside them. Sloping ceilings, alcoves, alternating two-roll half-drop hanging, and manufacturer-specific matching rules require a dedicated cutting plan.

## Standard wallpaper roll sizes and typical coverage

Retailers often price wallpaper per single roll while shipping bolts in double-roll lengths. Always enter the actual continuous roll length you will cut from.

| Roll format | Width | Length | Nominal area | Typical usable area |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| US single roll | 20.5 in (52 cm) | 16.5 ft (5.03 m) | 28 sq ft (2.6 m²) | ~20–22 sq ft |
| US double roll (most common) | 20.5 in (52 cm) | 33 ft (10.06 m) | 56 sq ft (5.2 m²) | ~40–45 sq ft |
| European / UK standard roll | 20.9 in (53 cm) | 33 ft (10.05 m) | 57 sq ft (5.33 m²) | ~42–48 sq ft |
| US wide double roll | 27 in (68.6 cm) | 27 ft (8.23 m) | 60.75 sq ft (5.64 m²) | ~45–50 sq ft |
| Commercial vinyl (Type II) | 54 in (137 cm) | Sold by linear yard | 13.5 sq ft / yd | Varies by drop |

## Step by step
1. Measure the width of each wall you plan to paper and add the widths together. Keep standard doors and windows in the total because full-height drops are still cut beside them.
2. Only measure and subtract wide openings such as sliding glass doors or large arched pass-throughs where whole vertical strips are genuinely skipped.
3. Measure ceiling height from the top of the baseboard or skirting board to the ceiling line at the tallest spot in the room.
4. Check the roll label for roll width, roll length, pattern match type (random, straight, or half-drop), and pattern repeat distance.
5. Allow roughly 4 in (10 cm) of total trim per drop for squaring the top and bottom edges during hanging.

## Common mistakes
- Dividing wall area by roll area. Area division ignores unusable off-cuts left at the end of every roll and frequently under-orders by 15% to 25%.
- Confusing a US single roll (sold priced per single roll, packed as a double roll) with the actual double-roll length you cut from.
- Forgetting half-drop pattern waste. An offset match shifts every second strip by half a repeat, which can reduce drops per roll from three to two.
- Ordering from multiple print runs. Always check that every roll shares the same dye-lot or batch number before hanging.

## Worked examples
### Example 1
Metric: a 10 m wall run, 2.4 m ceiling, 53 cm × 10.05 m rolls, 64 cm straight repeat, and 10 cm trim need 7 rolls (19 drops, 3 drops per roll).

### Example 2
US double roll: a 32 ft wall run, 8 ft ceiling, 20.5 in × 33 ft roll, 24 in straight repeat, and 4 in trim need 7 double rolls (19 drops, 10 ft cut length).

### Example 3
Plain design: the same 10 m × 2.4 m metric room with no repeat fits 4 drops per roll and needs 5 rolls.
